Space & Defense Daily — Tuesday, Oct 27, 2026

Recovered from the chat delivery: the wording is exact, but the original source links could not be recovered, so sources are shown as plain-text citations.

Here's your space and defense news for Tuesday, Oct 27.

Top stories: Europe's five biggest military powers pledged to carry more of NATO's load. Republican defense hawks warned that Trump's tilt toward Russia could sink his $1.5 trillion defense budget. And ESA ordered four more Galileo satellites.

NATO

  • NATO Deputy Secretary General Radmila Shekerinska joined the E5 defense ministers (France, Germany, Italy, Poland and the UK) in Paris. She urged allies to "dig deep and do more" on air defense for Ukraine through the program that buys US weapons for Kyiv. NATO
  • The E5 statement names Russia the most acute long-term threat. It says Europe must take more responsibility inside NATO, while still calling the US "indispensable." GOV.UK
  • European ministers and EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas warned that Putin isn't seeking peace, and Kallas expects a "brutal" winter for Ukraine. Politico Europe
  • NATO's Canadian-led brigade in Latvia started Resolute Reforger 2026, its biggest deployment drill yet. About 3,000 troops are taking part, through Nov. 2. Kyiv Independent
  • Britain won't join the Canada-led Defence, Security and Resilience Bank, a setback for the planned global defense bank. Defense News
  • Politico Europe lays out the open questions as the UK tries to deliver its promised defense spending increases. Politico Europe

European Union

  • The EU is pushing back on Starlink in five ways: backing the proposed Airbus, Thales and Leonardo space merger; reserving satellite spectrum for European companies; building the IRIS² constellation, with first launches now in 2029; offering Ukraine its Govsatcom secure-satellite service; the draft EU Space Act. Politico Europe
  • India's defence secretary says demand from the ReArm Europe plan is boosting Indian ammunition exports to Europe. Defense News
  • With 48 hours to go before the EU-Canada summit, member states still can't agree whether to call Canada an "associate member." Politico Europe
  • German defense startup Helsing unveiled its Contra air-defense system and two interceptors. They're built to chase Russia's fast Geran drones for under $100,000 per shot. Defense News and Breaking Defense

United States

  • The FY2027 defense bill (the NDAA) and full-year Pentagon funding are stuck until the lame-duck session. Sen. Mitch McConnell warned that "ending the obeisance to Mr. Putin may be table stakes" for Trump's end-of-year agenda. Roll Call
  • Breaking Defense lists the midterm races to watch for defense, since Democrats could flip one or both chambers. Breaking Defense
  • The Space Force wants commercial hardware for the space between Earth and the Moon ready to launch by 2029. Two industry requests are coming soon, plus a $30M Lunar Prime challenge. Air & Space Forces
  • The Air Force moved ARRW, its first hypersonic weapon, into production with a $694M Lockheed Martin contract. Air & Space Forces
  • The Air Force plans a $1B test campus at Nellis Air Force Base for the F-47 fighter. Air & Space Forces
  • The Air Force Research Laboratory used an Oct. 20 SpaceX rideshare to test moving cargo through space. Air & Space Forces
  • Anduril is going into laptop manufacturing with Qualcomm, aimed at government and military buyers. DefenseScoop
  • USS Colorado will be the first US submarine to join Submarine Rotational Force-West in Australia. Defense News
  • NASA ended the Swift observatory's mission after a rescue attempt failed, and Swift should reenter within weeks. Space.com
  • NASA is overhauling how it picks science missions, aiming for "more missions, more often." Space.com
  • SpaceX test-fired Super Heavy booster B22 ahead of its next Starship launch. Space.com
  • A Falcon 9 launched 27 Starlink satellites from Vandenberg at 12:25 AM PT today. Spaceflight Now

European space

  • ESA ordered four more second-generation Galileo navigation satellites from Airbus and Thales Alenia Space, bringing that fleet to 16. They're due in 2031, and the first launch of this generation is in 2028. ESA
  • ESA's Hera asteroid-defense spacecraft imaged the asteroids Didymos and Dimorphos as two separate objects for the first time. ESA
  • CRISTAL, the Copernicus ice-monitoring satellite, has its solar arrays fitted and is moving into testing. ESA

Global

  • A ceasefire brokered by Melania Trump began in Russian-occupied Oleshky to let aid in. Overnight, Russian missiles hit Kyiv and damaged the Southern Bridge. Euronews
  • Astroscale proposed a fleet of "bodyguard" spacecraft to protect satellites from attacks in orbit. Space.com
  • A Hudson Institute report says the Air Force should cap its KC-46 tanker buy and develop a new longer-range tanker to meet the China threat. Breaking Defense
